description: Frog wakes up in the desert! Hop through the desert, the Arctic, a forest and the ocean to find Frog's pond, and learn the four things every habitat gives.

youtube.title: Habitat Hop! Animal Homes for Kids: Desert, Arctic, Forest, Ocean, Pond | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Frog wakes up on hot sand: this isn't home! Ride the Habitat Hopper through the desert, the Arctic, a forest and the ocean, and find out why each one is wrong for Frog.
Meet a desert hare with big ears, a polar bear and its brown bear cousin, fish with gills, and finally Frog's pond. Every habitat gives food, water, shelter and space.
Try at home: make a habitat in a shoebox.

do.text: Habitat Hop
Hot sand? No pond? This isn't my home!
Hold on, Frog! The Habitat Hopper will find your way back.
And we'll find out why the desert is wrong for you.
Thank you, friends. I'm not hurt, just very puzzled!
A habitat is an animal's home.
habitat
A habitat can be huge, like an ocean, or small, like a pond.
Every habitat gives an animal four things.
Food to eat.
Water to drink.
Shelter, a safe place to rest and hide.
And space to move around and find food.
When I say every home needs,
you say food, water, shelter, space!
Every home needs...?
Food, water, shelter, space! Great.
And animals have bodies that fit their homes. Let's check.
At every stop, I'll tick the four needs on my checklist.
And you can help. Is each place a good home for Frog?
We're in the desert. It's hot and dry.
Fan yourself! Phew, it's hot.
Desert plants and seeds are food.
Water is very hard to find.
A cactus stores water in its thick stem.
Animals rest in burrows and in the shade, out of the sun.
Meet a desert hare. Look at those big ears!
Big ears let heat out of its body. That keeps it cool.
And the camel stores fat in its humps for long trips.
Is the desert a good home for Frog? What do you think?
But why can't Frog live here?
Fun fact: frogs don't drink with their mouths.
They soak up water through their skin!
In the dry desert, Frog's skin would dry out.
And there's no pond.
I need water! Next stop, please.
Brrr! The Arctic, far in the north. Ice and snow everywhere.
Shiver with Frog! Brrr!
Here lives the polar bear. A cousin of the brown bear.
My thick fur and a layer of fat keep me warm.
My big paws help me walk on snow and ice.
Polar bears eat fish and seals. They rest in snow dens.
Fun fact: under that white fur, polar bear skin is black!
Dark skin helps soak up the sun's warmth.
Is the polar home a good home for Frog?
And penguins? Do they live here too?
No! Penguins live far in the south.
They never meet polar bears.
It's much too cold for me. Frogs can't stay active here!
The forest! Lots of trees for shelter.
Here's the polar bear's cousin, the brown bear.
I eat berries, nuts, and fish from the stream!
My strong claws help me dig and climb.
Same kind of animal, different bodies for different homes.
different bodies
The squirrel hides nuts and sleeps in a tree.
Is the forest a good home for Frog?
Checklist. Food: berries and nuts. Water: streams.
Shelter: trees and caves. Space:
lots. Good home, for the bear.
Close! But I need my own pond.
Oops! I steered us into the ocean.
Swim with your arms! The ocean is the biggest home of all.
Fish breathe underwater with gills, and swim with fins.
gills
The whale is a big friend who comes up to breathe air.
Is the ocean a good home for Frog?
Food: fish and sea plants. Water:
yes, but it's salty sea water.
But ocean water is salty.
Fish can't live out of water,
and frogs can't live in the salty sea.
Salty water is wrong for frogs! Let's go!
My pond! I'm home!
Is the pond a good home for Frog?
Yes! Fresh water, not salty. Bugs and worms to eat.
Lily pads and reeds for shelter.
Water and a muddy bank for space.
Frog's wet skin, strong legs and webbed feet fit the pond.
Welcome home, neighbour! Quack!
Food, water, shelter, space.
All four. This is Frog's habitat.
The pond also has a safe place for frogs to lay their eggs.
And that's why I can't live in the desert!
Leap like a frog! Chant with us!
Hop, hop, where's your home?
Food and water, a place to roam!
Hot and dry for the desert hare,
ice and snow for the polar bear!
Trees and berries for the bear,
a pond for frogs, with fresh water there!
Hop, hop, where's your home?
Food and water, a place to roam!
Challenge! Three animals are in the wrong homes.
Shout where each one should go,
and the Hopper will beam it home.
A polar bear in the desert! What's wrong?
Too hot for thick fur! Send it home to the polar home.
A duck on the ice! What's wrong?
No open water to swim, and too cold! Send it to the pond.
A desert hare in the ocean! What's wrong?
It can't swim far, and there are no plants to eat.
Back to the desert!
Three rescues. Every animal is back where it fits.
A farm is not a wild habitat.
Farm animals live with people who care for them.
And remember: cows,
pigs and sheep live with people on farms.
Quiz time! What four things does every habitat give?
Food, water, shelter and space!
Why does a polar bear have thick fur?
To stay warm in the icy cold!
Where does Frog live?
In a pond, with fresh water!
Which home is hot and dry?
The desert!
Four for four! You're habitat experts.
Thank you for bringing me home!
Mission complete.
Make a habitat in a box at home. Bye from the pond!
